metadata.note: The Atlantic Coast Line's Champion, the New York-Miami streamliner that ran the coastal route Amtrak's Silver Meteor uses today. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; any place where the historical routing differed is described in the segment notes and reflected in the geometry. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones (train introductions, renamings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables. Added in response to a question about whether the Auto Train's Savannah-area route existed in 1900: yes, in pieces -- the Florida Special feature below models the same corridor from its 1888 debut, run jointly by RF&P, the pre-1900 Atlantic Coast Line constituent roads, Henry Plant's Savannah, Florida and Western Railway (not ACL-owned until the 1902 Plant System purchase), and the FEC. Its geometry reuses the exact same NY-Miami alignment as the Champion feature, since it is the same physical coastal route via Savannah.
sources: https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=28944 and american-rails.com RF&P entry (Florida Special debuted 1888 as an 'electric lighted, steam heated' joint train over RF&P + connecting roads)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Line_Railroad (ACL brand used by predecessor roads from 1871; Atlantic Coast Line Company holding formed 1893; formal merger into Atlantic Coast Line Railroad 1900; Plant System, including the Savannah-Jacksonville Savannah, Florida and Western Railway, purchased 1902)
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: ACL inaugurated the New York-Miami Champion in Dec 1939, months after rival Seaboard Air Line's Silver Meteor kicked off the Florida streamliner race. The Champion ran ACL's coastal route via Rocky Mount, Florence, Charleston and Savannah - the same alignment Amtrak's Silver Meteor uses today, and the one this geometry follows. (Seaboard's own Silver Meteor ran the rival inland route via Raleigh and Columbia, today's Silver Star routing.) estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The Florida Special debuted in 1888 as an 'electric lighted, steam heated' winter luxury train, a joint operation of the RF&P (Washington-Richmond), the constituent roads that would become Atlantic Coast Line in 1900 (Richmond-Charleston, via Petersburg/Weldon/Wilmington/Florence), Henry Plant's Savannah, Florida and Western Railway (Savannah-Jacksonville, part of the Plant System, not yet ACL-owned), and Flagler's FEC south of Jacksonville (see florida_east_coast_railway.geojson) -- the same coastal alignment via Savannah that Amtrak's Auto Train and Silver Meteor still use. Seasonal (winter-only) single train; frequency approximate.

segments.note: Atlantic Coast Line's 1902 purchase of the Plant System unified the whole Richmond-Jacksonville route under one company; the Florida Special continued as ACL/FEC's flagship winter train until superseded by the streamlined Champion in Dec 1939 (see the acl-champion feature in this file). Seasonal, single train; frequency approximate.
